court: High Court of Judicature at Madras

parties.respondent_defendant: Thilagavathi, Kanagavalli Ammal, Unnamalai Ammal, Sarasu Ammal, S. Durairaj (Respondents)

outcome_detected: the judgment of the Trial Court in O.S.No.11 of 1996 is confirmed
facts_of_case: Suit for partition filed by first respondent/plaintiff and one Appar against the defendants. The case is about dividing the suit properties into six equal shares and allotting 2/6 shares to the plaintiffs.

legal_principles.principle: Marriage has to be specifically pleaded and proved.
legal_principles.held: A faint attempt was made to show that since the Plaintiffs are admittedly the children of Subbarayulu Naidu born through their mother P.W. 2 the paternity is not in dispute.
cited_cases: Mohan & Mother vs. Santha Bai Ammal & Others, (1987) CDJ MHC 431

legal_principles.principle: Without pleadings and evidence in support of the pleadings, a valid marriage cannot be presumed.
legal_principles.held: The judgment 'Surjit Kaur vs Garja Singh & Ors reported in [1994-1-L.W.38]' is relied for the proposition that without pleadings and evidence in support of the pleadings, a valid marriage cannot be presumed.
cited_cases: Surjit Kaur vs Garja Singh & Ors, (1994) 1 LW 38

outcome.final_order: The judgment of the Trial Court in O.S.No.11 of 1996 is confirmed.
